check_math_010.patch_new:
THIN = r"(?:\s*\\[!,;:> ])*"
    SUB = r"(?:_\{[^}]*\}|_[A-Za-z0-9])"
    # ``\big``/``\Big``/``\bigg``/``\Bigg``, with the optional ``l``/``r``/``m`` suffix,
    # open a delimiter exactly as ``\left`` does, so ``E_t\bigl[\cdot\bigr]`` is the same
    # construction as ``E_t\left[\cdot\right]``. Explicit alternation, not an optional
    # brace: an opener is still required after it, so ``E \bigm|`` cannot backtrack into
    # a match.
    DELIM = r"(?:\\left|\\bigg?[lrm]?|\\Bigg?[lrm]?)"
    applied = (r"(?:\s*" + SUB + r"?" + THIN +
               r"\s*(?:" + DELIM + r")?" + THIN + r"\s*(?:\[|\\\{|\())")
    # Two juxtaposed shapes carry the operator with no delimiter at all, and neither is
    # ambiguous. ``E \sum``, ``E_0 \prod``: a letter applied to a big operator is an
    # operator, not a matrix factor. 56 occurrences, every one read, 0 false positives.
    bigop = r"(?:\s*" + SUB + r"?" + THIN + r"\s*\\(?:sum|prod)(?![A-Za-z]))"
    # ``E_t u_{t+1}``: a *subscripted* E juxtaposed with a subscripted symbol. The
    # subscript on E is what makes this safe — this corpus also uses E for a matrix, a
    # matrix of ones, expenditure and energy, and none of those is time-indexed. All 73
    # corpus matches (43 inside the gate, 30 outside it) are the operator.
    # Dropping the subscript requirement admits 39 more (``Eq_a`` in
    # ``hansen_jagannathan_1991``, ``E w_{st}`` in ``supply_demand_var``); those look
    # genuine too but were not audited one at a time, so they are left out.
    juxta = r"(?:\s*" + SUB + THIN + r"\s*[A-Za-z]" + SUB + r")"
    # ``\mathbb E \sum`` is kept out of all three by the mask below, not by a lookbehind
    # here: ``\mathbb`` + one space is not the only spelling (``lqramsey`` writes
    # ``\mathbb E  \sum``), and a fixed-width lookbehind would miss it and double-count.
    bare_E = re.compile(r"(?<![\\A-Za-z0-9_{])E(?:" + applied + r"|" + bigop
                        + r"|" + juxta + r")")
check_math_010.rationale:
The mechanism reproduces, and all three sub-shapes are sound; the reviewer's *totals* do not reproduce, because they silently depend on a second change the brief told me not to implement.

MEASURED, pattern only, gate untouched (348 lectures, Counter over (line, detail) per file):
A `\big`-family delimiters: +8 / −0, 4 file-paths (reviewer said +12).
B `E \sum` / `E \prod`: +56 / −0, 11 file-paths (reviewer said +91).
C `E_t u_{...}`: +43 / −0, 8 file-paths (reviewer said +29).
A+B: 1489 → 1553, +64 / −0, 13 file-paths, reach 124.
A+B+C (recommended): 1489 → 1596, +107 / −0, 16 file-paths, reach unchanged at 124.
A whole-CHECKS sweep confirms qe-math-010 is the only rule that moves.

WHY THE REVIEWER'S NUMBERS ARE BIGGER, AND WHY THEIR OWN FILED EVIDENCE STILL SCORES 0. Their two headline lines — `tax_smoothing_3.md:80` (`E_0 \sum_{t=0}^\infty \beta^t T_t^2`) and `un_insure.md:34` (`E \sum_{t=0}^\infty \beta^t \left[ u(c_t) - a_t \right]`) — are NOT among my 107 additions, and neither is `tax_smoothing_1.md:70`. In those files `e_is_operator` is False (no `E[`/`E\{` anywhere), so the whole bare-letter branch is switched off and no pattern change can reach them. This is the second half of the deliberate limitation in VERIFICATION.md, and the reviewer plainly patched it too: widening the gate to accept A- and B-shaped evidence flips 28 file-paths on and yields A+B+C = 1489 → 1657, +168 / −0, across exactly **33 distinct file-paths with 12 moving off zero** (7 basenames × their series copies: tax_smoothing_1/2/3, un_insure, lq_inventories, permanent_income_dles, supply_demand_var) — their 33 and their 12, to the number. So their reach claim is a gate claim wearing a pattern claim's clothes. Reported, not implemented, as instructed.

C IS SOUND — the scepticism does not survive measurement. I read all 43 additions individually. Every one is the expectation operator, and two lectures say so in their own prose: `cagan_rational_expectations.md:158` — "where $E_t x_{t+1}$ is the mathematical expectation of $x_{t+1}$ conditional on information available as of time $t$" — and `lqramsey.md:557` — "where $\tilde E_t$ is the conditional mathematical expectation". To probe the E-as-matrix risk directly I also ran C with the gate removed entirely: 73 matches corpus-wide, 43 inside the gate and 30 outside it (`amss2.md:554` `\beta E_{t-1} u_{c,t}`, `entropy.md:378` `q_t^1 = E_t m_{t+1}`, `supply_demand_var.md:927` `\hat E_{t-j} z_t`), and all 73 are the operator. Not one matrix, expenditure or energy E. The mandatory subscript on E is what buys that: a matrix E is not time-indexed.

WHAT I NARROWED, AND WHAT IT COST. C requires a *single Latin letter* after E's subscript, so `E_t\mu_{t+j}` (`cagan_rational_expectations.md:172`) and `E_t \beta^t`-style macro operands are still missed — the doubt filed the shape as `E_t u_{...}` and I implemented exactly that. B covers `\sum`/`\prod` only, not `\int`. And I kept the subscript on E mandatory: dropping it adds 39 more matches (`Eq_a`, `Ex_a` in `hansen_jagannathan_1991.md:340`, `Er_v^*` at :602, `Ev_t v_t'` in `hs_recursive_models.md:1429`, `E w_{st}^2 = .5` in `supply_demand_var.md:146`). Spot-checking those in context, they look genuine too, but 39 unaudited additions do not belong in a patch justified by a read of every one — that is a separate doubt.

ON THE GATE (report only). These forms *should* feed `e_is_operator`, and B is the one that matters. Widening the gate to A+B evidence: A+B → 1489 → 1601, +112 / −0, 30 file-paths, reach 124 → 136; A+B+C → 1489 → 1657, +168 / −0, 33 file-paths, reach 136, 12 paths off zero. I read the 61 additions that widening contributes and found no false positive either — `perm_income_cons.md:94`, `markov_jump_lq.md:94`, `supply_demand_var.md:112` (`E_t\Big\{`), `tax_smoothing_1.md:354` (`E_t T_{t+1} = (S-MF)(A-BF)x_t`). The cost is that reach jumps 12 and seven `lecture-dp`/advanced lectures stop scoring a clean 0 on this rule, which moves category scores; that is a scoring decision, not a detector decision, so it wants its own pass. Also worth noting for whoever takes it: the gate pattern is a hand-copied duplicate of `applied` that lacks the `THIN` steps, so simply reusing `applied` for the gate is itself worth +1 (one more file's gate flips on `E_0\!\left\{`) before any of A/B/C is considered — a small latent inconsistency between the gate and the branch it guards.

check_code_002.patch_old:
# A Greek name almost never stands alone in this corpus: it carries a subscript or a
# plural — ``mu_0``, ``phi_pi``, ``Sigma_x``, ``alphas``, ``sigmas``. The old trailing
# ``(?![\\w])`` counted only the bare word, so a lecture writing ``mu_0=μ_sim_0`` on one
# line was reported clean. The suffix is consumed rather than merely allowed, so
# ``m.end()`` is the end of the whole identifier and the kwarg tests below still work.
# ``chi2`` is deliberately left out: a trailing digit is not a subscript here, it is
# scipy's chi-squared.
GREEK_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.])(" + "|".join(GREEK_WORDS) +
                      r")(?:s|_[A-Za-z0-9_]+)?(?![A-Za-z0-9])")
check_code_002.patch_new:
# A Greek name almost never stands alone in this corpus: it carries a subscript, a
# plural, or an English prefix — ``mu_0``, ``phi_pi``, ``Sigma_x``, ``alphas``,
# ``target_mu``, ``c_gamma``, ``n_thetas``. Allowing a *suffix* was only half of it: the
# lookbehind rejects a preceding ``_``, so the Greek word still had to come first.
# ``mu_vec`` was caught and ``target_mu`` was not, on the same line —
# ``hansen_richard_1987.md:658`` is ``def mv_weights(mu_vec, Sigma, target_mu)`` — and
# ``os_egm_jax.md:368``, ``c_gamma, x_gamma = solve_model_crra(..., γ)``, two spelled-out
# ``gamma``s beside the unicode one, was reported clean.
# The pattern therefore spans the *whole* identifier: ``_``-joined segments before the
# Greek word and the remainder after it. Matching the whole identifier is what keeps one
# identifier to one occurrence (``rho_chi`` stays a single ``rho`` hit, not two) and keeps
# ``m.end()`` at the end of the identifier, so the keyword-argument and assignment tests
# below still work. The leading group is lazy so the *first* Greek segment is the one
# named, which leaves every existing detail string unchanged.
# ``chi2`` is deliberately left out: a trailing digit is not a subscript here, it is
# scipy's chi-squared. That guard is an explicit ``(?![A-Za-z0-9])`` immediately after the
# Greek segment — placing it after the trailing group instead would let the engine
# backtrack past it.
GREEK_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w.])(?:[A-Za-z0-9]*_)*?(" + "|".join(GREEK_WORDS) +
                      r")s?(?![A-Za-z0-9])(?:_[A-Za-z0-9]*)*(?![\w])")
check_code_002.rationale: The mechanism reproduces exactly: the canonical site os_egm_jax.md:368 `c_gamma, x_gamma = solve_model_crra(..., γ)` is now 2 hits, and hansen_richard_1987.md:658 `def mv_weights(mu_vec, Sigma, target_mu)` stops contradicting itself within one line. Whole-identifier matching (the reviewer's guard 1) is not an extra guard but the mechanism itself, and it needs nothing else: 700 -> 815, reach 57 -> 71, +115 / -0 across 23 file-paths, 14 newly reached, every canary intact. What I dropped is guard 2. Its blanket form ("skip identifiers the file def's") deletes the market_diffusion.md:159 `def mu(self, a)` canary — measured, 8 removals — which is the exact exemption this project already rejected. Narrowing it to mixed English/Greek identifiers still deletes 7 HEAD findings (theil_2.md:622 `def beta_tilde(σ, β_hat_val, α_sq_val)`, cagan_rational_expectations.md:431 with `ρ = rho_from_moments(...)` fourteen lines later, risk_aversion_or_mistaken_beliefs.md:1353 `def xi_function(self, x): return x @ self.Ξ @ x`), and narrowing it further to distribution-named def's still deletes theil_2's four. That fails the both-directions test in every form. The cost of dropping it: 45 additions the reviewer would have silenced survive — Greek words inside English function-name phrases such as `compute_res_wage_given_beta(β)` and `s_from_psi(ψ)`. I judge those real and consistent, since the rule already counts `def beta_tilde(σ, ...)` and `def rho_from_moments(σ_ε2, ...)` at HEAD and two of the new ones sit on a line that also writes the unicode form (two_computation.md:1036 `τ_l = _find_ss_tau_l(`). It also lets 13 genuine false positives in, listed above. `tv_beta` is not one of them and is not a finding: merging_of_opinions.md computes the total-variation distance between two posterior **Beta** distributions (`tv_distance_beta` at :536) and imports `from scipy.stats import beta as beta_dist`, so the existing file-level import exemption already keeps all 3 occurrences out — verified absent from the 115. Guard 2 is therefore wrong in kind; the FP class worth a follow-on is `mu` for marginal utility. A separately measured gate — skip a non-bare `mu` identifier in a cell that binds `u_prime`/`marginal_utility`, in the style of the existing DIST_CALL gate — is surgical: it drops exactly those 12 additions plus the 4 identical FPs already at HEAD (815 -> 799, reach 71 -> 67) and touches nothing else. I left it out of this patch to keep the change to one contiguous site; apply it separately if wanted.

check_ref_001.patch_new:
# A hand-written author-year immediately followed by a plain ``{cite}`` for the same
# work renders the reference twice over — "Shavell and Weiss (1979) [Shavell and
# Weiss, 1979]" (``un_insure.md:17``). The fix is ``{cite:t}`` *alone*, replacing the
# hand-written name, so the finding carries its own wording. This branch is
# deliberately *not* subject to the clause-end exemption: the duplication is rendered
# wherever the citation sits, so it does not decide the open narrative/parenthetical
# question in ``contributions/issues/06-ref-001-author-name-citations.md``. The guard
# requires a capitalised token immediately before the parenthesis (an author surname)
# and a four-digit year in 1600–2099, so ``equation (1979)`` and ``(1234)`` cannot
# match; the lookbehind stops the capital being taken from inside a lowercase word.
# +39 occurrences over 20 lectures, 0 removed. Loosening the guard to any non-space
# character adds one more, ``black_litterman.md:546`` (``> (1978) {cite}`…`)``), where
# the surname is on the previous line — measured and left out.
AUTHOR_YEAR_CITE = re.compile(
    r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9])[A-Z][^\s(]*\s*\((?:1[6-9]|20)\d\d[a-z]?\)\s*\{cite\}`")
